name: HivePunk 547
subject: Pollen Robotics Microduck
thesis: Microduck is a credible open sim-to-real platform because its full onboard stack, MuJoCo training code, simulator and ONNX policies are published and actively committed, but its value as a buyable physical robot remains unproven until retail units ship and are independently tested.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: pollen-robotics/microduck has 50 raw commits in the last 30 days, 35 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is c375fee, on 2026-11-18.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Microduck is described as a 25 cm open-source biped you train yourself with reinforcement learning.
claims.quote: A 25 cm open-source biped you train yourself with reinforcement learning.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Pre-orders are listed at $399 before taxes and shipping, opening August 27, 2026.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The SDK, simulation and full RL training stack are on GitHub.
claims.quote: The SDK, the simulation and the full RL training stack are on GitHub.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The whole software stack is Apache-2.0 licensed.
claims.quote: Apache-2.0 The whole software stack, permissively licensed

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The onboard repo runs daemons on a Rockchip RK3566 with a 50 Hz control loop driving fifteen servos from neural policies.
claims.quote: About 25 cm and 800 g of robot, run by a handful of daemons on a Rockchip RK3566: a 50 Hz control loop driving fifteen servos from neural policies

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Policies are trained in microduck_rl using MuJoCo and PPO, with ONNX export loaded by the microduck repo.
claims.quote: The policies it runs are trained next door, in microduck_rl — MuJoCo and PPO, the sim2real recipe, and the export to ONNX that this repo loads.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: scripts/duck-sim runs the real daemons against a body in MuJoCo, one duck in a window or four as machines you log into.
claims.quote: scripts/duck-sim runs the real daemons against a body in MuJoCo — one duck in a window, or four as machines you log into.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Pollen published the shipped policies to the Hub as microduck-policies on 31 August 2026, ten of them now.
claims.quote: Pollen published the shipped policies to the Hub as microduck-policies on 31 August 2026, ten of them now, with velstand the default walk since 14 September.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Microduck's software is open source and its hardware is not.
claims.quote: Its software is open source and its hardware is not

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Pollen publishes no CAD, circuit boards or bill of materials for the robot itself.
claims.quote: Pollen publishes no CAD, circuit boards or bill of materials for the robot itself.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The robot is pre-hardware, with pre-orders open and shipping targeted for December 2026, and almost nobody outside Pollen has a physical unit yet.
claims.quote: The robot is pre-hardware: pre-orders are open, shipping is targeted for December 2026, and almost nobody outside Pollen has a physical unit yet.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The microduck repo has 50 raw commits in the last 30 days, 35 of them real work, with latest real commit c375fee on 2026-11-18.

risks: Software is open source but hardware is not, and Pollen publishes no CAD, circuit boards or bill of materials for the robot itself.
The robot is pre-hardware for most people, with shipping targeted for December 2026, so hardware-facing tools are mostly pre-validation and have not been exercised on shipped retail units.
Split licensing for 3D model files is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 non-commercial, which limits commercial replica use.

Policy distribution and hardware-facing MCP servers, gateways and CLIs are written against published design docs and simulators, with few exceptions tested on development boards or community replicas.
Price is an introductory pre-order price before taxes and shipping, and final delivery timing and availability are not confirmed by the pages.
wouldChangeMind: Confirmed retail shipments with independent hands-on testing of policies on shipped units.
Publication of hardware designs, CAD, schematics or a bill of materials, or an independent security audit of the update system.
Evidence that simulator-trained policies fail to transfer reliably, or that pre-order delivery dates slip substantially.
